text:
Maya: FYI ran a long-run profile on the kv cache with a realistic long-context workload, saw steady memory growth and higher fragmentation than expected.
Sam: can you paste the profiler output?
Maya: pasted excerpt below — this is from a 6h soak with mixed tenants + chatty long prompts:
```
PROFILE: kv_cache resident_bytes=2.34GB evicted_bytes=158MB entries=1.02M fragmentation=27%
hot_prefixes=3.2k distinct_prefix_hashes=98k avg_entry_size=2.4KB
largest_buckets: tenant:acct-42 prefix_hash:0x1f2a size:120MB entries:18k
```
Maya: fragmentation is weird — lots of small free gaps. eviction rate spikes during bursts and then resident_bytes never falls all the way.
Leon: that smells like variable-sized entries + LRU churn. We allocate KV pages per entry size class, but we don't coalesce freed slots across sizes, so holes accumulate.
Akiko: Are prefixes stored verbatim as cache keys? if so we may be storing extremely long keys for some prompt templates which increases avg_entry_size.
Maya: yes — current key format: `<tenant_id>::<session_id>::<prefix_raw>` (we keep raw prefix for exact match).
Sam: that explains it. Two issues: 1) different sessions with same effective prefix produce distinct keys (low reuse), 2) raw prefix length variance -> fragmentation.
Leon: propose normalizing key: `<tenant>::<prefix_hash>` and keep session stickiness as an optional separate mapping. That reduces key length and allows reuse across sessions when acceptable.
Akiko: +1 but we need rollout guards. Some customers rely on strict session isolation. We should make normalization opt-in per tenant and expose a "session_stickiness" flag.
Maya: Also observed eviction waterfall: when a big tenant bursts, we evict many small entries first but the big long-prefix entries persist causing page-level fragmentation. We should switch to size-aware eviction (LRU per size bucket + global aging).
Sam: Another option: store a compact fingerprint for the prefix (BLAKE2/64) + a short modality tag to avoid collisions. That keeps key fixed length.
Leon: Implementation sketch:
```text
KEY_V2 = b32(tenant_id) + ":" + hex(blake2_64(prefix_normalized))
If tenant_sticky == true:
  session_map[(tenant, session)] -> set of key_v2 references (weak refs)
Eviction: per-size LRU + global reclaim that prefers evicting large contiguous blocks first
```
Akiko: We should also add prefix normalization rules: strip trailing whitespace, canonicalize whitespace, mask non-deterministic tokens (timestamps, ids) via simple regex heuristics. Provide a sanitize mode that can be toggled.
Maya: Did a quick sim replacing keys with 64-bit hashes and merging by tenant: resident drops ~18%, fragmentation down to 12%, hit-rate up ~6% on chatty longctx workload.
infra-bot: deploy-canary started: runtime-kv-v2 on canary pool (canary-3)
Sam: Good. For telemetry: add metrics for key_collision_count, normalization_rate, per-tenant reuse_rate, avg_entry_size_by_prefix_hash.
Leon: We should be careful with accidental collisions — blake2_64 is low risk but add a fallback: when fetching a key, verify prefix equality for corner cases (store short checksum).
Akiko: Also add a TTL sliding-window for prefixes: if prefix was used within X minutes extend; otherwise allow cross-session reuse. Configs: tenant default TTL=10m, sticky-mode=false.
Maya: Action items:
- Maya: push prototype key_v2 + normalization to branch (I'll open PR)
- Leon: prototype size-aware eviction policy in simulator and run long soak
- Sam: add telemetry + unit tests for collision fallback + config flags
- Akiko: coordinate with security/compliance about tenant opt-in for cross-session reuse
Sam: timeline?
Maya: aiming for canary PR today, soak for 48h, then small production ring if numbers look good.
Leon: will run simulator overnight with synthetic longctx traces and report fragmentation traces tomorrow.
Akiko: will draft config change doc for Console and API so tenants can toggle stickiness and normalization.
Maya: thanks — ping me if you need the raw profiler output. I'll attach the full trace in the PR. :thumbsup:
